---
title: Styles
---

This is how we can add styles or representations of our molecular data, so we can actually see something.

```{python}
import molecularnodes as mn

cv = mn.Canvas(resolution=(860, 540), transparent=True)
```


```{python}
codes = ["4ozs", "8H1B", "6N2Y"]
styles = ["cartoon", "ribbon", "surface"]

for code, style in zip(codes, styles):
    mol = mn.Molecule.fetch(code)
    mol.add_style(style, material="MN Flat")
    cv.frame_object(mol, viewpoint="right")
    cv.snapshot()
    cv.clear()

```

```{python}
mol = (
    mn.Molecule.fetch("8H1B")
    .add_style("cartoon", material = "MN Ambient Occlusion")
    .add_style(
        style="surface",
        selection="protein",
        material="MN Transparent Outline"
        )
)
cv.frame_object(mol)
cv.snapshot()
```


```{python}
with mol.tree.reset() as (atoms, join):
    (
        atoms
        >> mn.nodes.geometry.StyleRibbon(
            selection=mn.nodes.geometry.IsPeptide(),
            peptide_radius=1.5,
            quality=5,
            material=mn.material.append_material("MN Ambient Occlusion")
        )
        >> mn.nodes.geometry.StyleSurface(
            selection=mn.nodes.geometry.IsPeptide(),
            material=mn.material.append_material("MN Transparent Outline")
        )
        >> join
        
    )
cv.snapshot()
```


```{python}
cv.clear()
cv.engine = mn.scene.Cycles(samples=32)
mol = (
    mn.Molecule.fetch("9EYM")
    .add_style("cartoon",  selection = "is_peptide", material = "MN Ambient Occlusion",)
    .add_style("ball_and_stick", selection = "not protein", material = "MN Default", bond_find = True)
)

cv.frame_view(mol)
cv.snapshot()
```

```{python}
cv.frame_view(mol, (-3.14, 0, 0))
cv.snapshot()
```
